key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that MgSiO₃ post-perovskite conducts lattice heat 44–55% better than bridgmanite under matched lower-mantle conditions.
engineering_relevance: This computational geoscience study—not solar-cell research—provides thermal-conductivity inputs for modeling lower-mantle heat transport and core cooling.
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Combine phase-boundary and geotherm calculations with aggregate conductivity bounds.
evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, substituting DFT forces for MACE forces changes calculated conductivity by only 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
watch_item: The core–mantle boundary aggregate estimate of 9.5–11.4 W/(m K) assumes Fe-free minerals and 80 vol% silicate plus 20 vol% MgO, limiting direct extrapolation to realistic mantle compositions.
paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
